Explained answers and corrections

Unit 1 · Week 16 · Lesson 2 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open the exam-preparation chapter and its learning resources. Use paper or a local editor as appropriate, with fictional data and disposable practice copies. The suggested 55-minute lesson is flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Explained answers and corrections

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Explain the goal and the expected independent outcome. Use explanations to identify why a response needs repair. This is ungraded textbook learning. Suggested times can be adjusted to the class. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

2. Retrieval and explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual retrieval, then partner comparison

A first attempt shows the original reasoning. A correction should identify what changed and why, not simply replace it with the answer. Allow silent thinking before discussion. Ask a learner to justify an answer before revealing the explanation. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

3. A correction record

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked table and teacher explanation

Use the public explained answers. Equivalent valid reasoning is acceptable. Avoid scores and grade predictions. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

4. The boundary at 50

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Predict, model and explain

Correct charges are 5, 0, 0. The strict greater-than version fails only the exact-boundary case among these three. Pause for predictions before discussing the expected result. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

5. A response with missing evidence

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

A suitable example pairs Application with a web protocol or service role. A label alone may leave part of the prompt unanswered. Swap explaining and checking roles so both learners articulate the reasoning. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

6. Independent practice

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application with optional support

Use teacher feedback for course diagram symbols and coherent alternative designs. Self-checking cannot certify every drawing convention. Offer the relevant worked example if needed, then use a changed case to check independent understanding. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

7. A choice to explain

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Whole-class response and justification

A. Ask the learner to explain the rule in their own words before trying fresh data. Give thinking time and collect reasons, without recording scores. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.

8. Exit explanation

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Individual reflection and fresh explanation

A good response identifies the cause and demonstrates the repair with changed values or conditions. Use the response to select the next explanation or practice activity. Teaching reference: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#exam-preparation. Use the current chapter and its linked resources.
